body:
Addition from the reporter's first try (2026-11-23): the app must also explain how to get a key, in plain steps, next to "Set API key...". The reporter did not know what a key is or where to get one. For Anthropic:
1. Sign in at the Anthropic console, then open Settings > API keys.
2. Click Create key. Give it a name, for example "CamCraft on <computer>", so that you can revoke only this key later.
3. Copy the key at once. It starts with `sk-ant-`, and the console shows it only once.
4. Paste it into "Set API key...".
5. Keep it secret, like a password. To stop it, delete it on the same page.
6. Cloud use costs credits. Link to the billing page and its spend limit.

Give the same short steps for OpenAI and Gemini (Google AI Studio), and for Ollama a "how to install a model" line.

Replacing a key must also work. The Terminal workaround fails on a second store ("The specified item already exists in the keychain"). It needs `security add-generic-password -U ...` to update the stored key. "Set API key..." must replace a stored key without an error.

More for the user-facing explanation (reporter, 2026-11-23: "this info should be explained to the user"). Put it in the app, next to the key setting, and on a guide page (`site/content/guide/`, AI Chat setup):
- On the first Send after the key is stored, macOS asks: 'CamCraft wants to use your confidential information stored in "camcraft-ai" in your keychain. To allow this, enter the "login" keychain password.' Say what this is. The password is normally the Mac login password. Choose **Always Allow**. **Allow** grants one read, so the prompt comes back on every Send.
- The app is not code-signed, so macOS can ask again after an update. This is expected.
- Windows (Credential Manager) and Linux (Secret Service) show their own prompts or none. Describe each one briefly.
claimed: Codex (m3) · 2026-11-23 23:54:46 UTC · branch mkinney:issue/3781-ai-key-setup · plan: Add secure key setup, provider readiness, and setup guidance.

User-facing "how to get a key" text for the remaining providers (reporter's request, 2026-11-23: capture these instructions in the issue). Use it in the in-app help next to "Set API key..." and on the guide page, with the Anthropic steps above.

**Gemini (Google)**
- A Gemini app subscription (Gemini Pro / Google One AI) does **not** include an API key. The key comes from Google AI Studio with the same Google account, and its free tier covers normal chat use.
- Steps:
  1. Go to aistudio.google.com and sign in.
  2. Accept the terms (first time only).
  3. Click **Get API key**, then **Create API key**. If AI Studio asks for a Google Cloud project, let it create a default one.
  4. Copy the key. It starts with `AIza`.
  5. Paste it into "Set API key..." for Gemini.

**OpenRouter** (once the custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint from #3783 exists)
- Steps:
  1. Go to openrouter.ai, sign in, and open **Keys**.
  2. Click **Create key**, then copy it.
  3. Add credits if the models you want are not free.
  4. In CamCraft, use base URL `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with that key.

**OpenAI**
- A ChatGPT subscription does not include an API key either. Create the key at platform.openai.com > API keys, and add billing.

**Ollama (local, free, no key)**
- Install Ollama from ollama.com, then `ollama pull <model>`. Show the recommended models from #3789 here.
- For the current benchmark leaders, see that issue. Very small models (for example phi4-mini) cannot change a project reliably.

**Terminal fallback** until the in-app button exists (macOS):
- Store a key: `security add-generic-password -U -s camcraft-ai -a <anthropic|openai|gemini|openrouter> -w`. It asks twice and shows nothing. `-U` replaces a stored key.
- Remove a key: `security delete-generic-password -s camcraft-ai -a <name>`.
- The first Send asks for the login keychain password. Answer **Always Allow**.

Correction to the Gemini steps above: do not tell users the key starts with `AIza`. A new AI Studio key (2026-11-23) used a different prefix and was accepted. Say only "Copy the key". Also, do not validate Gemini keys by prefix in the app; check them with a request.

Ollama setup text for users (reporter, 2026-11-23: "tell the users how to start it up, and if they need to specify a port or common command line options"). Use it in the in-app help and on the guide page:

**Install**
- macOS / Windows: download the app from ollama.com and start it. It runs in the menu bar / system tray and starts the server.
- Homebrew alternative on macOS: `brew install ollama`.
- Linux: the install script on ollama.com sets up a `systemd` service: `systemctl status ollama`.

**Start the server** (if the app is not running)
- `ollama serve`.
- It listens on **http://localhost:11434**. CamCraft's "Offline local (Ollama)" uses exactly that address (`http://localhost:11434/v1`), so most users need no settings.
- **Check that it runs:** `curl http://localhost:11434/api/version` or `ollama list`. CamCraft's status line says "Ollama not running at <url>" when this fails.

**Get a model**
- `ollama pull <model>`.
- Prefer models that can call tools; see #3789 for the recommended ones. Small models (for example phi4-mini) cannot change a project reliably.
- `ollama list` shows what is installed. The Model field must match a name from that list exactly.

**Common options** (environment variables, set before `ollama serve`, or in the app's settings)
- `OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11500`: use another port. CamCraft must then be pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:11500/v1`. Today the panel has no field for this; see #3783.
- `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434`: serve other computers on the network, for example a GPU box. **Warning:** anyone on that network can then use it. Point CamCraft at `http://<that-computer>:11434/v1`.
- `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768`: CamCraft sends its whole tool list with each request. The default context window of many models is too small, so the model forgets or truncates the tools. Use a larger context (memory permitting).
- `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=30m`: keeps the model loaded between messages, so each Send does not wait for a reload.

Note for #3783: the app already has presets for Unsloth Studio (`http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`), LM Studio (`http://localhost:1234/v1`) and llama.cpp `llama-server` (`http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`, start with `--jinja` for tools) in `crates/app/src/ai/presets.rs`. The AI Chat provider list does not show them, and there is no base-URL field. Expose them, give each the same short start-up note, and add a base-URL field.
